baseState.general: A third-generation platinum analog. It is a cornerstone in the treatment of colorectal cancer, typically administered as part of the FOLFOX chemotherapy regimen.
baseState.mechanism: Like Cisplatin, it undergoes aquation but at a slower rate. It features a large, bulky DACH (diaminocyclohexane) ligand, which completely alters its pharmacological profile and prevents cross-resistance.
baseState.sideEffects: Unlike Cisplatin, it is much less toxic to the kidneys and ears. Its primary dose-limiting side effect is acute, cold-induced peripheral neuropathy (nerve pain triggered by cold).
baseState.clinical: Administered intravenously. Often combined with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and leucovorin. Patients are strictly advised to avoid cold drinks and exposure to cold air for 3-5 days post-infusion.

dnaState.general: Forms bulky, hydrophobic DNA cross-links that are structurally distinct from those formed by Cisplatin, making it highly effective against Cisplatin-resistant tumors.
dnaState.mechanism: Binds N7 of guanine residues forming 1,2-intrastrand crosslinks. The bulky DACH ligand protrudes into the major groove of the DNA, creating a rigid, narrower bend that causes extreme structural distortion.
dnaState.sideEffects: DACH-platinum adducts block DNA polymerase and RNA transcription. NER attempts repair; unrepaired lesions trigger p53-dependent apoptosis and mitotic catastrophe.
dnaState.clinical: Mismatch Repair (MMR) proteins fail to recognize the DACH-distorted DNA adducts. This prevents the cancer cell from initiating repair bypass mechanisms, permanently halting DNA synthesis.
